title: RAC artifact-spec registry element
description: One element of the artifact_specs array in artifact-specs.json: the complete, language-neutral description of one artifact type. Every built-in type is an element of this shape, and a corpus-pinned spec bundle (SPEC.md section 6.1 and 6.5) is a JSON object whose artifact_specs array holds elements of this shape. Object key order is significant wherever the description says so; an implementation preserves it. The shape is append-only: new fields are optional and appended, and existing fields keep their meaning.

name.description: The canonical type key, used as the frontmatter type value, the family directory name (<name>s), and the schema/templates key. Lower-case, starts with a letter, 2 to 32 characters; never the reserved word unknown. A bundle element whose name is a built-in's is skipped: built-ins always win.

display.description: The human label (Requirement, Decision, Runbook). Non-empty.

required.description: Sections that define the type, each scored 1 point by the classifier and required by validation. Normalised section names: trimmed, lower-case, single-spaced, in declared order. Non-empty.

recommended.description: Expected-but-optional sections, scored one half point and reported as missing recommended by validation. Declared order.

optional.description: Recognised sections that are never scored and never reported missing; this is where a type lists the relationship sections it may carry (related decisions, related requirements, related tickets, ...). Listing a relationship section admits it as a source of references; it does not make the type a valid relationship target and adds no relationship type.

metadata.description: Section name to its closed vocabulary of allowed values, in declared order (for example status to [Proposed, Accepted, Superseded]). Values are matched case-insensitively and reported in their canonical spelling.

retired_status.description: The subset of metadata.status values that mark a retired artifact (Superseded, Deprecated). Each entry must appear in metadata.status when both are present.

descriptions.description: Section name to a one-line description rendered by schema output, in declared order.

guidance.description: Section name to the prompt lines rendered as comments in a starter template and offered by improve, in declared order.

synonyms.description: Alternative heading (normalised) to the canonical section it maps to, applied before section matching for this type only.

id_field.description: A section that carries the artifact's canonical identifier when frontmatter is absent. No built-in sets it; null when unused.

starter_bodies.description: Section name to the starter text a new artifact of this type is scaffolded with, in declared order. A bundle type has no template file: its template is rendered from required and recommended sections, starter bodies, and guidance.

okf_type.description: Appended, optional. The OKF type an export writes for artifacts of this type. Absent on the built-ins, whose mapping is the fixed table in the OKF profile (requirement to Requirement, decision to ADR, roadmap to Roadmap, prompt to Prompt, design to Design, risk to Risk). A bundle element that omits it exports under its display. Non-empty when present.

section.description: A normalised section name: trimmed, lower-case, single-spaced, as the classifier compares headings after normalisation.
